match.reason: No point in the bank covers how income and wealth are distributed in Australia; the closest, costs of growth, only mentions inequality as one possible cost of growth.

rejected.title: Inequality in Australia
card: In Australia, wealth is spread much less evenly than income. A small share of households holds a large share of all wealth, and the poorest households hold very little.
Wealth is built up over many years through saving and through rises in the value of assets. So older households usually hold more wealth than younger ones.
Women on average earn less than men and have lower superannuation savings when they retire. Average incomes and wealth also differ between cities, regional areas and remote areas.
On average, First Nations Australians have lower income and wealth than other Australians. These are averages, so many individuals differ from them.
rejected.remember: Australian wealth is more unevenly spread than income, and averages also differ by age, gender, location and First Nations status.

a.q: Which statement about the spread of income and wealth in Australia is correct?
opts: Wealth is more unevenly spread than income
Income is more unevenly spread than wealth
Income and wealth are equally unevenly spread
Wealth is evenly spread, but income is not
a.why: Wealth builds up over time and a smaller share of households holds most of it, so it is more unequal than income. The reverse is tempting because people see wages every week, but wealth is the more unevenly spread.
a.clue: Think about which one builds up over many years.

b.q: Jo is 62 and Sam is 26. They earn the same income. Which is the best reason Jo is likely to hold more wealth?
opts: She has had longer to save and gain from assets
She has a higher yearly income than Sam does
Wealth is set only by which area a person lives in
Older workers are always paid higher wages than younger ones
b.why: Wealth builds up over time through saving and rising asset values, so older households usually hold more. The option about higher income is wrong because Jo and Sam earn the same income.
b.clue: The incomes are equal, so look at how wealth is built.
